2608.30103.title: Graph4BiLO: Graph Neural Network Approximation for Bilevel Mixed-Integer Linear Optimization
2608.30103.paper_summary: Bilevel mixed-integer linear optimization problems model hierarchical decision processes in which a leader anticipates the optimal response of a follower. Although expressive, these problems are computationally challenging because lower-level optimality is embedded in the leader's feasible region. Value-function reformulations replace the nested follower optimization with a constraint involving the follower's optimal value, but evaluating this value function exactly can itself be expensive. This paper introduces Graph4BiLO, a graph neural network (GNN) approach for learning bilevel value functions from variable--constraint graph representations. In contrast to fixed-length multilayer perceptron (MLP) representations, the GNN uses shared message-passing parameters and can therefore be applied across multiple problem sizes with a single trained model. The learned ReLU network is encoded exactly as mixed-integer linear constraints and embedded in an approximate single-level formulation. A repair step subsequently re-solves the follower problem for the selected leader decision to recover a bilevel-feasible follower response. We evaluate Graph4BiLO on knapsack interdiction instances with 20--100 items against the exact MibS solver and the learning-based Neur2BiLO method. Graph4BiLO obtains objective values comparable to Neur2BiLO across all tested sizes while avoiding size-specific neural networks. An additional out-of-distribution experiment demonstrates zero-shot transfer from 20-item training instances to previously unseen 40- and 60-item instances. However, embedding message passing at every graph node substantially increases the resulting mixed-integer formulation size and solve time. These results identify a central tradeoff between size-generalizable graph representations and the computational cost of embedding GNNs within optimization models.
2608.30103.paper_summary_zh: 雙層混合整數線性優化問題模型化了層級決策過程，其中領導者預測跟隨者的最佳反應。雖然這些問題表達能力強，但由於下層的最優性嵌入在領導者的可行區域中，因此計算上具有挑戰性。價值函數重構用涉及跟隨者最優值的約束取代了嵌套的跟隨者優化，但準確評估這個價值函數本身可能代價高昂。本文介紹了Graph4BiLO，一種從變量-約束圖表示中學習雙層價值函數的圖神經網絡（GNN）方法。與固定長度的多層感知器（MLP）表示相比，GNN使用共享的消息傳遞參數，因此可以在多個問題大小上應用單一訓練模型。學習到的ReLU網絡被精確編碼為混合整數線性約束，並嵌入到近似的單層公式中。隨後，一個修復步驟重新解決選定領導者決策的跟隨者問題，以恢復雙層可行的跟隨者反應。我們在20-100個物品的背包干預實例上評估Graph4BiLO，並與精確的MibS求解器和基於學習的Neur2BiLO方法進行比較。Graph4BiLO在所有測試大小中獲得的目標值與Neur2BiLO相當，同時避免了特定大小的神經網絡。一個額外的分佈外實驗展示了從20個物品的訓練實例到之前未見的40和60個物品實例的零樣本轉移。然而，在每個圖節點嵌入消息傳遞會大幅增加最終的混合整數公式大小和求解時間。這些結果確定了大小可泛化的圖表示與在優化模型中嵌入GNN的計算成本之間的中心權衡。
